findings.reason: the attribution source has to change (the ledger row §3 calls durable, or the committed run record) or the pass has to run before the same pass prunes the directory; otherwise a node implements exactly what §8 says and leaves a class of copies unbounded.
findings.text: the settling pass selects a directory only when "its run directory records that the run ended (its exit record or a discard marker)", but §3's landed retention predicate (`_run_directory_retention_report`, reckon/crew/gc.py) prunes a finished run's directory purely by mtime grace and consults no scratch copy, and §7's `retention_sweep` prunes those same directories in the pass that §8 makes the hourly caller. So a copy sitting on a host that runs no launch and no step within that grace window loses its only attribution source, falls under "a directory with no such record keeps today's handling", and is then removed only by `garbage_collect_orphan_scratch` — which §1 itself says nothing schedules. The plan states "Every other copy is removed on its own host by a settling pass", which its own §3 makes untrue for that residue.

findings.reason: the four are re-derivable from the durable release records of the 62 promoted runs, so the node can identify them without the plan naming ids; the defect is traceability, not the measure.
findings.text: "the route of each of the named four unexplained survivors" names four runs the plan never identifies: the measured runs it does name are the single 29-record example and the two review runs, and "Four of the 62" (line 169) is a count with no ids.

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — every case is measurable, but one requirement names "the named four unexplained survivors" that the plan never names (line 170); the rest, including the negative control, can fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate logs sit "under the run directory" and the fragment under the evidence store, both on the shared crew home; the fixtures the cases use are temporary by design, not the delivered logs.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test file is named for the mechanism, and no symbol, comment or path carries a plan label, ticket number or version tag.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the settling pass attributes a copy through the run directory, which §3's landed retention pass deletes after its grace window, so the two routes disagree about what evidence outlives a run.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §8 has one deliverable, a run's scratch removed on every host that holds it; the record-reading is a prerequisite of that one fix, not a second outcome.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §8 declares `depends-on: crew-state-stays-bounded#s7`, which is the landed `retention_sweep` §8 extends, and no relationship points at a node that does not exist.
